projects.title: COWCPU — Custom RV32I RISC-V Processor
projects.stack: Verilog · RISC-V · Icarus Verilog · GTKWave · Vivado · Zybo Z7-10
projects.summary: A custom 32-bit RISC-V processor designed from the RTL level in Verilog, progressing from individual CPU components to a working multi-cycle RV32I processor and a 5-stage pipelined architecture.
projects.oneLiner: A 32-bit RISC-V processor built from the RTL up
projects.overview:
COWCPU is a custom 32-bit RISC-V processor developed from scratch to explore processor architecture, RTL design and FPGA implementation.

The project began with individual components such as the ALU and progressed into a working multi-cycle RV32I processor. Development is now continuing toward a 5-stage IF/ID/EX/MEM/WB pipeline, with later plans for hazard handling, forwarding, peripherals, performance monitoring and FPGA deployment on the Zybo Z7-10.
projects.role: Designed and implemented the processor architecture and RTL, including the ALU, datapath, control logic and instruction execution. Developed testbenches and used waveform-level debugging to verify processor behaviour while progressing from individual modules to a complete multi-cycle core and pipelined architecture.

projects.title: Axon-Hillock spiking neuron
projects.stack: SKY130 · SPICE · Analog IC Design · Layout · DRC / LVS
projects.summary: Analog tapeout project implementing an Axon-Hillock spiking neuron model on the Sky130 open-source PDK.
projects.imageAlt: Oscilloscope-style trace for an analog spiking neuron project
projects.oneLiner: A silicon spiking neuron designed from the transistor level up.
projects.overview:
Axon-Hillock is an analog IC project exploring the implementation of a biologically inspired spiking neuron in the SKY130 process.

The circuit is being developed from schematic-level design and transistor simulation toward physical layout, DRC/LVS verification and post-layout characterisation. The longer-term goal is to prepare the design for fabrication and evaluate how closely measured behaviour matches pre-layout and post-layout simulations.
projects.role: Responsible for the circuit architecture, transistor-level implementation, simulation and verification of the neuron design. The project also covers the physical IC flow, including layout, DRC/LVS and post-layout analysis as development progresses.

projects.title: AXI4-Lite FIR filter accelerator
projects.stack: Verilog / SystemVerilog · AXI4-Lite · FPGA · Vivado · RTL Simulation
projects.summary: A hardware FIR filtering accelerator implemented in RTL and integrated through an AXI4-Lite interface for processor-controlled configuration and operation.
projects.oneLiner: A memory-mapped FPGA accelerator for hardware FIR filtering.
projects.overview:
This project implements a finite impulse response (FIR) filter as a dedicated RTL hardware accelerator, with an AXI4-Lite interface providing processor-accessible control and configuration.

The project explores the connection between digital signal processing and SoC hardware design, including FIR datapath implementation, fixed-width arithmetic, memory-mapped register interfaces and RTL verification.
projects.role: Designed and implemented the FIR processing datapath and AXI4-Lite interface, integrated the accelerator into the RTL design, and verified register transactions and filter behaviour through simulation and waveform analysis.

projects.title: CDC-safe asynchronous FIFO
projects.stack: Verilog · CDC · FIFO · Cocotb · Icarus Verilog · GTKWave
projects.summary: A dual-clock asynchronous FIFO designed for reliable data transfer between unrelated clock domains, using Gray-code pointer synchronization and full/empty protection logic.
projects.oneLiner: A robust dual-clock FIFO for safe data transfer across asynchronous clock domains.
projects.overview:
This project implements an asynchronous FIFO for transferring data safely between independent write and read clock domains.

The design uses Gray-coded read and write pointers, multi-stage synchronizers and full/empty detection logic to reduce clock-domain-crossing risk and provide reliable FIFO operation under unrelated clock frequencies.
projects.role: Designed and implemented the FIFO RTL, including dual-port storage, binary and Gray-code pointer logic, clock-domain synchronizers and full/empty flag generation. Developed verification to exercise asynchronous read/write behaviour and inspected internal pointer and flag transitions using simulation waveforms.

projects.title: High-Throughput Pipelined AES-128 Accelerator
projects.stack: Verilog · AES-128 · FPGA · Vivado · RTL Simulation
projects.summary: Fully pipelined AES-128 implementation with CI-gated linting, simulation, and coverage.
projects.oneLiner: Fully pipelined AES-128 implementation with CI-gated linting, simulation, and coverage.
projects.overview:
This project implements the AES-128 symmetric encryption algorithm as a pipelined RTL architecture for FPGA.

The design explores how cryptographic operations can be mapped into dedicated digital hardware, with the AES transformation stages organised to support increased processing throughput compared with a purely sequential implementation. The project combines cryptographic algorithm implementation, RTL design, pipelining and FPGA verification.

projects.title: Dual ADS8568 FMC Carrier Board
projects.stack: Altium Designer, ADS8568, Nexys Video (Artix-7), FMC-LPC, REF6025
projects.summary: A 4-layer mixed-signal FMC carrier board digitising 12 conditioned analogue channels for an FPGA-based motor-dynamometer DAQ.
projects.imageAlt: Dual ADS8568 FMC carrier board project preview
projects.oneLiner: A 4-layer mixed-signal FMC carrier board digitising 12 conditioned analogue channels for an FPGA-based motor-dynamometer DAQ.
projects.overview: Interfaces two ADS8568 16-bit simultaneous-sampling SAR ADCs to a Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA over the FMC-LPC connector. Accepts twelve conditioned 0-10 V analogue channels, protects and buffers each ADC input, and routes the parallel data and control buses to the FPGA for deterministic 200 kS/s acquisition. Part of an MEng motor-dynamometer DAQ replacing a prior microcontroller design limited by channel skew and throughput.
specs: 24 V in -> 5 V analogue, 3.3 V digital (from FMC)

detail.heading: Architecture
detail.body: Sits between the analogue sensor boards and the FPGA. Conditioned 0-10 V signals enter via D-Sub, pass through buffering, RC filtering and ADC-input protection, then reach the two ADS8568 devices. The FPGA drives conversion-start, read and reset lines and reads back the parallel data/status buses through FMC-LPC.

detail.heading: Design decisions
detail.body: Chose the ADS8568 (true-bipolar, simultaneous-sampling SAR) over delta-sigma and pipeline alternatives because the motor waveforms are PWM-like and demand low-latency, phase-coherent multi-channel sampling. External REF6025 reference, jumper-selectable, for ADC accuracy.

detail.heading: Implementation
detail.body: 4-layer mixed-signal stack-up for controlled grounding and clean power distribution. Analogue input section physically separated from the digital section; analogue traces kept short and direct; FMC-LPC connector positioned to mate mechanically with the Nexys Video board.

detail.heading: Challenges & solutions
detail.body: Shared CONVST/RESET across both ADCs handled with OR-gated reset logic. TVS protection on the 24 V rail. JTAG deliberately omitted since no components are JTAG-capable, using the 0 Ω bypass convention for the mezzanine.
